input_documents.content:
Point of View (POV) Document: Archestra AI Platform 
Executive Summary 
Archestra is an open-source AI platform that enables individuals, teams, and enterprises to 
connect multiple AI models, MCP tools, knowledge sources, and AI agents through a single 
secure interface. Rather than being an AI model itself, Archestra acts as a central control 
layer that helps organizations manage AI applications, agents, security, governance, 
integrations, and observability from one platform.  
In simple terms: 
Archestra is a central platform where users can connect AI models, MCP servers, tools, 
data sources, and AI agents, and manage them from a single location. 
What is Archestra? 
Archestra is an all-in-one Enterprise AI Platform designed to help build, deploy, manage, 
secure, and scale AI-powered applications and agents. It provides: 
• AI Chat Interface 
• LLM Gateway 
• MCP Gateway 
• MCP Registry 
• Agent Runtime 
• Knowledge Base (RAG) 
• Security Guardrails 
• SSO & RBAC 
• Monitoring & Observability 
• Environment Management 
These capabilities allow businesses to deploy AI securely while maintaining governance, 
visibility, and control. 
What Is Archestra Used For? 
Organizations use Archestra to: 
Internal AI Assistants 
Provide employees with AI-powered assistants that can access company knowledge and 
answer questions. 
AI Agent Automation 
Create AI agents that can: 
• Process emails 
• Generate reports 
• Analyze documents 
• Trigger workflows 
• Respond to events 
Multi-Model AI Access 
Provide access to multiple AI providers through a single gateway. 
Enterprise Knowledge Search 
Allow employees to search internal documents using AI-powered retrieval.  
MCP-Based Tool Access 
Connect AI systems with enterprise tools through MCP servers and registries.  
AI Models Supported 
Archestra supports multiple AI providers through its LLM Gateway. Users generally need to 
bring their own API keys. Archestra provides the management and routing layer but is not 
itself an AI model provider.  
OpenAI 
• GPT-4o 
• GPT-4.1 
• Embedding Models 
Anthropic 
• Claude Sonnet 
• Claude Opus 
• Claude Haiku 
Azure OpenAI 
• Any GPT deployment available in Azure 
Amazon Bedrock 
• Claude Models 
• Llama Models 
• Mistral Models 
• Amazon Nova Models 
DeepSeek 
• DeepSeek Chat 
• DeepSeek Reasoner 
MCP Capabilities 
Archestra includes: 
• MCP Gateway 
• MCP Registry 
• MCP Orchestrator 
• Private MCP Catalog 
• OAuth-Based Authentication 
These capabilities allow organizations to centrally manage MCP servers and tools.  
MCP Servers That Can Be Connected 
Development Tools 
• GitHub 
• GitLab 
• Bitbucket 
Project Management 
• Jira 
• Azure DevOps 
• Linear 
Collaboration 
• Microsoft Teams 
• Slack 
Knowledge Management 
• SharePoint 
• Confluence 
• Notion 
• Google Drive 
Databases 
• PostgreSQL 
• SQL Server 
• MySQL 
• MongoDB 
Enterprise Platforms 
• Dynamics 365 
• Salesforce 
• SAP 
• ServiceNow 
Custom Systems 
• Internal APIs 
• Proprietary Business Applications 
• Custom MCP Servers 
Any MCP-compliant server can potentially be integrated into Archestra.  
Data Sources That Can Be Ingested 
Archestra's RAG and Knowledge Base capabilities allow ingestion of multiple data sources.  
Files 
• PDF Documents 
• Word Documents 
• PowerPoint Files 
• Excel Files 
• Text Files 
Knowledge Repositories 
• SharePoint 
• Confluence 
• Notion 
• Google Drive 
Enterprise Systems 
• CRM Data 
• ERP Systems 
• Databases 
• Data Warehouses 
Online Sources 
• Websites 
• APIs 
• Documentation Portals 
This information can then be used by AI assistants and agents to provide contextual 
responses.  
Agent Capabilities 
One of Archestra's primary strengths is its Agent Runtime. Users can build their own custom 
AI agents.  
Types of Agents 
Personal Assistant Agents 
Examples: 
• HR Assistant 
• IT Support Assistant 
• Employee Helpdesk 
Research Agents 
Examples: 
• Market Research Agent 
• Competitive Intelligence Agent 
• Web Research Agent 
Document Processing Agents 
Examples: 
• Contract Review Agent 
• Invoice Processing Agent 
• Compliance Review Agent 
Automation Agents 
Examples: 
• Report Generator 
• Email Processing Agent 
• Ticket Management Agent 
Multi-Agent Systems 
Examples: 
• Planner Agent 
• Research Agent 
• Writer Agent 
• Reviewer Agent 
The platform supports sub-agent delegation where one agent can assign tasks to another 
specialized agent.  
Build Your Own Agents 
Users can create custom agents that: 
• Use GPT, Claude, or other models 
• Call MCP tools 
• Access enterprise knowledge 
• Trigger workflows 
• Execute scheduled tasks 
• Process incoming emails 
• Respond to API/webhook events 
• Collaborate with other agents 
Example Workflow: 
1     Project Manager Agent 
2             
| 
3             
4             
5             
+-- Research Agent 
| 
+-- Data Analysis Agent 
| 
+-- Report Writer Agent 
| 
+-- QA Review Agent 
6             
7             
8             
9             
This enables sophisticated multi-agent business automation.  
Tools That Can Be Connected 
Through MCP and integrations, agents can use external tools.  
Microsoft Ecosystem 
• Microsoft 365 
• Outlook 
• Teams 
• SharePoint 
Development 
• GitHub 
• GitLab 
• Azure DevOps 
CRM & Business Applications 
• Salesforce 
• Dynamics 365 
• ServiceNow 
Storage Platforms 
• SharePoint 
• OneDrive 
• Google Drive 
Communication Platforms 
• Teams 
• Slack 
• Email Systems 
Custom Tools 
• Internal APIs 
• Business Applications 
• Proprietary Systems 
Security & Governance Features 
Archestra includes enterprise-grade controls such as: 
• Single Sign-On (SSO) 
• OIDC 
• SAML 
• Entra ID Integration 
• Okta Integration 
• Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) 
• Secrets Management 
• AI Guardrails 
• Dual-LLM Verification 
• Lethal Trifecta Protections 
These features help organizations maintain security and compliance while adopting AI.  
Monitoring and Cost Control 
Archestra provides built-in observability features: 
• OpenTelemetry Tracing 
• Prometheus Metrics 
• Logging 
• Usage Monitoring 
• Per-Team Cost Tracking 
• Cost Limits 
• Environment-Based Controls 
This enables organizations to monitor and optimize AI usage.  
Pricing and Licensing 
Archestra follows an Open Core licensing model.  
Free Tier 
• Free for teams with fewer than 30 users.  
Enterprise Licensing 
• Available for larger deployments. 
• Enterprise pricing is not publicly listed. 
• Organizations must contact Archestra for a custom quote.  
Additional Costs 
Users should consider: 
• Cloud Infrastructure 
• Storage 
• Databases 
• Kubernetes Hosting 
• OpenAI API Costs 
• Claude API Costs 
• Azure OpenAI Costs 
• Other Model Provider Costs 
Archestra does not eliminate model costs; it helps manage and govern them.  
Local Setup Guide 
Prerequisites 
Install: 
• Docker 
• Docker Engine 
Step 1: Pull the Image 
1     docker pull archestra/platform:latest 
Step 2: Run Archestra 
1     docker run \ 
2     -p 127.0.0.1:9000:9000 \ 
3     -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \ 
4     -e ARCHESTRA_QUICKSTART=true \ 
5     -e ARCHESTRA_BETA=true \ 
6     -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \ 
7     -v archestra-postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \ 
8     -v archestra-app-data:/app/data \ 
9     archestra/platform 
Step 3: Open the Application 
Open: 
1     http://localhost:3000 
Step 4: Configure AI Models 
Add API keys for: 
• OpenAI 
• Azure OpenAI 
• Anthropic Claude 
• DeepSeek 
• Bedrock-supported models 
Step 5: Create Agents and Knowledge Bases 
• Connect knowledge sources 
• Register MCP servers 
• Configure AI models 
• Create custom agents 
• Build workflows

variables.system_message:
You are the Context Analyzer Agent in a PRD-generation workflow.

Your task is to analyze the provided source document and extract only information explicitly stated or directly supported by the document. Do not invent, infer, or embellish business facts.

Extract the following:
- Problem statement
- Business goal
- Evidence supporting the problem or goal
- Primary and secondary users
- Assumptions
- Constraints
- A concise context summary

For evidence, preserve important facts, metrics, examples, quotes, dates, and source references where available. Clearly distinguish documented facts from assumptions and missing information.

If information is missing, use null for singular values and an empty array for lists. Do not use placeholder prose.

Return valid JSON only. Do not include Markdown, explanations, comments, or code fences.

Use exactly this JSON structure:

{
  "problem_statement": {
    "summary": "",
    "details": [],
    "source_references": []
  },
  "business_goal": {
    "summary": "",
    "details": [],
    "success_definition": [],
    "source_references": []
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "type": "metric|fact|quote|example|observation|other",
      "statement": "",
      "value": null,
      "source_reference": "",
      "confidence": "high|medium|low"
    }
  ],
  "users": [
    {
      "user_type": "primary|secondary|unknown",
      "name": "",
      "needs": [],
      "pain_points": [],
      "source_references": []
    }
  ],
  "assumptions": [],
  "constraints": [],
  "context_summary": "",
  "missing_information": [],
  "analysis_metadata": {
    "document_name": "",
    "document_type": "",
    "analyzed_sections": [],
    "overall_confidence": "high|medium|low"
  }
}
variables.user_prompt:
Analyze the following source document and return the required JSON object.

Document name:
{{document_name}}

Document type:
{{document_type}}

Document content:
{{document_content}}

Instructions:
1. Extract the problem statement, business goal, evidence, users, assumptions, constraints, and context summary.
2. Preserve measurable evidence and source references whenever available.
3. Do not add information that is not supported by the document.
4. Put unresolved or missing details in "missing_information".
5. Return valid JSON only, using the exact schema defined in your system instructions.

variables.system_message:
You are the PRD Generator Agent.

Your task is to generate a complete Product Requirements Document using the supplied context analysis and the provided PRD template.

Follow Macy's Way of Working:
- Focus on business outcomes, measurable value, customer impact, and iterative delivery.
- Connect requirements to business objectives and measurable success criteria.
- Clearly distinguish facts, assumptions, constraints, and open questions.
- Do not invent product, stakeholder, technical, metric, timeline, or compliance information.
- When required information is unavailable, write "Not provided in source" or add the item to the Open Questions section.
- Do not silently convert assumptions into facts.
- Keep the PRD specific to the supplied context.

Complete every section of the template. Preserve the template's section order and headings. Replace template placeholders with supported information. Where a section cannot be completed, provide a concise statement explaining that the information was not provided.

Requirements must be testable and written with clear acceptance criteria using Given, When, and Then format.

Success metrics, targets, baselines, dates, owners, and release milestones must only be included when supported by the source. Otherwise, mark them as TBD or Not provided in source.

The final response must contain only the completed PRD in Markdown. Do not include analysis, commentary, implementation notes, or code fences.
variables.user_prompt:
Generate the completed PRD using the supplied template and context analysis.

PRD template:
{{prd_template}}

Context analysis:
{{context_analysis}}

Additional requested changes or reviewer feedback:
{{requested_changes}}

Instructions:
1. Use the context analysis as the primary source of truth.
2. Populate all sections of the PRD template.
3. Include the extracted problem statement, business goal, evidence, users, assumptions, and constraints.
4. Convert supported business goals into measurable objectives, outcomes, KPIs, leading indicators, and OKRs.
5. Define an appropriately scoped MVP and identify future enhancements separately.
6. Write functional requirements with business value and Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
7. Include user journeys, solution considerations, non-functional requirements, dependencies, risks, assumptions, open questions, milestones, epics, and release strategy.
8. Do not fabricate missing details. Mark them as "Not provided in source", "TBD", or include them under Open Questions.
9. Apply any valid requested changes without contradicting the source context.
10. Return only the completed Markdown PRD.

# Product Requirements Document (PRD)

## Title
[Product Name]

## Author
[Author Name]

## Date
[Date]

## Problem Statement
Customers are experiencing difficulties in navigating the online shopping platform, leading to increased cart abandonment rates and decreased customer satisfaction.

## Business Goal
To enhance the online shopping experience, reduce cart abandonment rates by 20% within the next quarter, and improve customer satisfaction scores by 15%.

## Evidence
Current analytics show a cart abandonment rate of 70% and customer satisfaction scores averaging 3.5 out of 5.

## Users
- Primary: Online shoppers aged 18-45
- Secondary: Customer support representatives

## Assumptions
- Users have access to the internet and are familiar with online shopping.
- Users prefer a streamlined and intuitive shopping experience.

## Constraints
- Limited budget for development and marketing.
- The project must be completed within the next quarter.

## Measurable Objectives
- Reduce cart abandonment rate from 70% to 50% by [Date].
- Increase customer satisfaction scores from 3.5 to 4.0 by [Date].

## Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
- Cart abandonment rate
- Customer satisfaction score
- Average time spent on the site

## Leading Indicators
- User engagement metrics (click-through rates, time on site)
- Feedback from user testing sessions

## Objectives and Key Results (OKRs)
- **Objective**: Improve the online shopping experience.
  - **KR1**: Achieve a 20% reduction in cart abandonment.
  - **KR2**: Increase customer satisfaction scores by 15%.

## Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
- A redesigned checkout process that simplifies user navigation and reduces the number of steps to complete a purchase.

## Future Enhancements
- Personalized product recommendations based on user behavior.
- Integration of a live chat support feature.

## Functional Requirements
1. **Redesigned Checkout Process**
   - **Business Value**: Streamlines the purchasing process, reducing friction for users.
   - **Acceptance Criteria**:
     - **Given** a user is on the checkout page, **when** they complete their information, **then** they should be able to proceed to payment without additional prompts.

2. **User Feedback Mechanism**
   - **Business Value**: Collects user feedback to continuously improve the shopping experience.
   - **Acceptance Criteria**:
     - **Given** a user completes a purchase, **when** they are prompted for feedback, **then** they should be able to submit their feedback easily.

## User Journeys
1. User visits the site, browses products, adds items to the cart, and completes the checkout process.
2. User encounters an issue during checkout and uses the feedback mechanism to report it.

## Solution Considerations
- Ensure the new design is mobile-responsive.
- Maintain compliance with data protection regulations.

## Non-Functional Requirements
- The system should load within 2 seconds.
- The checkout process should be accessible to users with disabilities.

## Dependencies
- Integration with existing payment gateways.
- Coordination with the marketing team for user communication.

## Risks
- Potential resistance to change from existing users.
- Technical challenges in integrating new features with the current platform.

## Open Questions
- What specific features do users find most frustrating in the current checkout process?
- What is the budget allocated for this project?
- Who will be responsible for user testing and feedback collection?

## Milestones
- Completion of design mockups by [Date].
- User testing phase begins on [Date].
- Launch of the redesigned checkout process by [Date].

## Epics
1. User Experience Redesign
2. Feedback Collection Implementation

## Release Strategy
- Roll out the MVP to a small segment of users first to gather initial feedback before a full launch.

## Conclusion
This PRD outlines the necessary steps to enhance the online shopping experience, aiming to reduce cart abandonment and improve customer satisfaction through a streamlined checkout process. Further details and clarifications are needed to finalize the project scope and execution plan.
